notes: Behavioural eval cases. These test whether the SKILL produces a correct, verified artifact — not whether the prose sounds nice. Run each prompt, then grade the produced HTML against its assertions. Assertions marked "script" can be checked mechanically; the rest need a human or LLM grader.

evals.name: mechanism-with-motion
evals.prompt: 用图解帮我真正理解：TCP 三次握手为什么是三次而不是两次
assertions: The artifact is a single self-contained .html file that opens offline with no network access
It contains at least one inline <svg> with an accessible name (<title> or role=img + aria-label)
If motion is used, it encodes a real state change (packet sent / state transition), not a decorative fade or pulse
A prefers-reduced-motion:reduce branch exists and yields the static final state
It explains why two handshakes are insufficient (stale duplicate SYN), not just that three happen
check_html.py --strict exits 0

evals.name: analogy-boundary-discipline
evals.prompt: Explain database indexes to me properly — I want to actually get it, not just a hand-wave
assertions: The analogy (e.g. book index / table of contents) is explicitly marked as an analogy
The artifact states at least one place where the analogy stops being accurate
A concrete worked example appears with values that correspond exactly to any visual quantities shown
The artifact states a real limitation (write cost, storage, or when the index is not used)
check_html.py --strict exits 0

evals.name: verification-honesty
evals.prompt: 用 ELI5++ 解释什么是缓存穿透
assertions: The delivery message names exactly which validation tiers ran
It does NOT claim visual or geometry verification if check_geometry.py was not run (or returned exit 2)
check_html.py --strict exits 0
If the artifact contains <script>, check_js.py exits 0
The delivery message ends with no more than one concise sentence outside the artifact

evals.name: scope-refusal-multitopic
evals.prompt: 用图解一次讲清 TCP、UDP、QUIC 三个协议，还有 TLS 握手，全部放一页
assertions: The response recognises this is a multi-topic request, not a single-concept explainer
It either narrows to one topic, or explicitly hands off to a curriculum skill (learn-in-3-hours)
It does not cram four unrelated mechanisms into one page while claiming one-scene-one-relationship discipline
check_html.py --strict exits 0 on whatever artifact it does produce
